chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: Kay Starr's $6,500 ring and the club's closing
summary: Hal Stanley wanted Kay Starr's ring to keep the club open another week; she refused and the club closed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: As a matter of fact, there's a funny story about it. Hal wanted to keep the place opened one more week, and he had given her an engagement ring that cost $6500, you know? So I was in the office with him this night, and he was saying, 'Kay, you got to let me have the ring, I think if I get off the nut this week, I really think I'll be able to stay open.' You know, and she says, 'I'm not gonna give you my ring, because ....' and I'm sitting there between them, you know, and so he says, 'Well, Lee, talk to her; see if you can't get the ring.' I said, 'If she was my wife, I'd get the ring, when she goes to sleep tonight, I'd cut that her finger off!'
Ooh! And didn't get the ring?

No, he didn't get the ring, and the place closed that week, too; you know, he couldn't meet the obligations. But that was a heck of a club; everyone hated to see it go -- the musicians and the performers hated to
see that club close, because that was something else. You remember the Mills Brothers used to work there all the time.
They were there when it was the Florentine Gardens.
